svg.data-steps: ["Seven kinds of healer in the 1890s, all of them selling to the same public. Regulars competed with homeopaths, eclectics, hydropaths, Thomsonians, patent medicine sellers and magnetic healers, and the boundaries between these groups were argued about far more than they were enforced.","Between the healer and the patient sits the licensing gate, which in principle decides who may treat the sick. In practice the statutes were narrow, unevenly enforced, and full of definitional gaps about what counted as the practice of medicine.","So the lanes run straight through. Where the practical requirements to begin treating patients were a room, a shingle and a willingness to be sued, every one of these sects reached the same patients, and the question of who counted as a legitimate healer stayed open.","That vacuum is the structural reason a new sect could take root at all. Chiropractic in 1895 did not have to defeat the gate, only to walk through the gap. And because the gate was legal from the beginning, the fight over chiropractic was legal from the beginning too, which is why so much of this history happens in courtrooms and statehouses rather than in journals."]
svg.aria-label: In the 1890s regulars, homeopaths, eclectics, hydropaths, Thomsonians, patent medicine sellers and magnetic healers all reached patients through the same weak licensing gate, so a new sect could pass straight through it too.

g.data-tip: The physicians of the day, organized and credentialed, but with a limited therapeutic arsenal and without the cultural authority they would hold fifty years later. Hearing the word irregular and supplying the word fraudulent imports a settlement that had not yet occurred.

Treated with very highly diluted remedies, chosen because at full strength they would produce in a healthy person the symptoms the patient already had. A rival system with its own schools and its own patients, not a fringe of one.
Built their practice on botanical remedies and, as the name says, claimed the right to take whatever seemed to work from any school rather than commit to a single doctrine.
Put water at the center of the cure: baths, packs, wraps and compresses, usually joined to a regimen of plain living. Like the others here, a drugless system with a single organizing agent.
Followers of Samuel Thomson's botanical system, which was sold as something a household could apply for itself. Its selling point was that you did not need to pay a physician at all.

Bottled proprietary remedies sold direct to the public on the strength of advertising, with the formula kept secret and often no examination of the patient at all. The lane that needed no practitioner in it.

Held that a vital force in the body could be depleted or restored by the direct action of a skilled operator's hands. D.D. Palmer made his living this way through the 1880s, so he came to 1895 already committed to an inner force running through the body.

The newcomer, and the only lane on this drawing that did not exist yet. What it added was a claim the neighbors did not make: that interference with nerve transmission at one named vertebral site is the general cause of disease. A distinct mechanism is a distinct territory.

g.text: the new sect uses the gap
licensing gate: weak, and mostly gaps
